title: A rumour about Aisha
hook: A necklace went missing, a caravan left without her, and a lie spread through Madinah for a month.

screens.text: **A necklace went missing.** A caravan left without her. And a lie about her spread through Madinah for a month. This is the story of how Allah Himself cleared her name.

**Left behind.** A few years after the hijra, Aisha, the Prophet's ﷺ wife, was travelling home with the army. She stepped away, found her necklace was gone, and went back to search. The army moved on, not knowing she wasn't in her litter [Bukhari 4750].
bubbles: Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal, travelling behind the army, found her. He spoke no word to her beyond a prayer, and led his camel, with her riding, back to the army [Bukhari 4750].

cards.back: Hypocrites, led by 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, turned an innocent delay into a lie about her [Bukhari 4750; Q 24:11].
Some sincere believers repeated it. That's how gossip spreads: through good people who don't stop it [Bukhari 4750].
Aisha. She fell ill for a month after they got home, and had no idea what people were saying [Bukhari 4750].

screens.text: **Heartbroken.** When she finally heard, she wept for days and couldn't sleep. For a month, no revelation came about it. Asked to speak, she said all she had was the beautiful patience of Ya'qub, Yusuf's father [Bukhari 4750].
bubbles: That's **sabr**: not pretending it doesn't hurt, but leaving her case with Allah.

screens.text: From a lost necklace to a cleared name.

events.text: Safwan finds her and leads her back to the army in silence [Bukhari 4750].

events.text: Hypocrites start it; some believers repeat it; she's ill and unaware [Bukhari 4750].

events.title: She finds out
events.text: She weeps, and answers with patience [Bukhari 4750].

events.title: Allah clears her
events.text: Verses come down declaring her innocent [Q 24:11].

screens.text: **Allah answers.** Verses came down declaring her innocent and calling out the lie: *"Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you"* [Q 24:11, Saheeh Intl.]. Then a question to everyone who had heard it.
bubbles: Told to go and thank her husband, Aisha said she would thank no one but Allah, who had cleared her [Bukhari 4750].

screens.prompt: A story about someone reaches you. Pass it on, or stop it?

items.text: Saying "I don't know that's true, and it's not ours to share"
items.why: That's Q 24:12: think well of each other and refuse what you can't prove.

items.text: Forwarding a screenshot "just so you know"
items.why: That's how good people spread a lie: one forward at a time.

items.text: Checking with the person directly, privately
items.why: Verify before you act on news [Q 49:6].

items.text: Asking "have you heard what they're saying about her?"
items.why: Even a question can pass on the rumour.

screens.text: **Your honour matters to Allah.** New Muslims are often talked about: at work, in the family, even at the masjid. Islam takes your reputation seriously. And it asks you not to pass on what you can't prove about anyone else.
bubbles: Day 63 covered words that build. Talking about people behind their backs, **ghibah**, is something the Qur'an warns against strongly [Q 49:12].

options.feedback: Yes. Think well of her, refuse the rumour, and don't pass it on. That's Q 24:12.

options.feedback: Not quite. Digging for details keeps the rumour alive. Stop it gently instead.

options.text: Warn other sisters, just in case

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- A few years after the hijra (during or after the campaign against Banu al-Mustaliq), returning from a campaign, Aisha went looking for a lost necklace; the army left without noticing she wasn't in her litter; Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal found her and brought her back, saying nothing to her beyond "inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" [Bukhari 4750].
- Hypocrites, led by 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, spread a lie about her; some believers repeated it [Bukhari 4750; Q 24:11].
- She was ill for a month and unaware; when she found out she wept for days. Revelation didn't come for a month. She answered with the "beautiful patience" of Yusuf's father [Bukhari 4750].
- During that month the Prophet ﷺ consulted people close to him and said publicly that he knew nothing but good about his family [Bukhari 4750].
- Allah revealed her innocence and rebuked those who spread it, in a passage of Surah al-Nur that begins at Q 24:11 [Q 24:11; Q 24:12]. Told to thank him, she said she would thank only Allah [Bukhari 4750].

**Likely questions**
- *"How old was Aisha?"* Only if asked, and never raised by the guide. The sahih reports in Bukhari and Muslim give six at the contract and nine when the marriage began [Bukhari 5133]; she became one of Islam's greatest scholars; norms of that time differed and his enemies never objected; some Muslim researchers argue for an older age while others defend the narration. Don't deny the hadith or mock the question. Offer the imam. (scholar question Q37)
- *"Did the Prophet ﷺ doubt her?"* Keep to the hadith: he consulted, waited for revelation, and said publicly he knew only good of his family. Don't speculate about his inner state.
- *"People are gossiping about me."* Listen first. Islam protects reputation; they don't need to defend themselves to everyone; talk to the mentor; if it's harassment or threatens safety, follow the safety rule.
- *"What does the Qur'an say about gossip?"* Verify news [Q 49:6]; avoid suspicion and backbiting [Q 49:12]; truthfulness [Bukhari 6094]; Day 63.
- *"Who was Aisha?"* One of the Prophet's ﷺ wives and a great scholar who narrated much of what we know of his life. Episode 40 covers his family.

**Escalate:** questions about Aisha's age beyond the outline above (Q37); questions about his marriages generally (Q41 territory, covered in episode 40).

**Don't**
- Don't raise Aisha's age or put it on any screen.
- Don't retell the accusation in any detail or make it salacious; it's about rumour, trust and Allah's vindication.
- Don't name the believers who repeated it.
